title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with synthetic video. An AI generated deepfake was used on a WhatsApp video call to make the caller appear as a sitting chief minister, and the fabricated identity was the whole basis of the request that followed. The false claim was not a stray model error but the working part of the scheme: the victim believed he was dealing with a public official offering aid, and every later demand for fees rested on that belief.

The failure sits at the point where a consumer messaging app connects two people with no verification of who is on either end. Nothing in the call established that the person on screen was the person he claimed to be, and the money moved through a digital payment app rather than through any channel tied to a government office. Catching it would have required the victim or the platform to confirm the caller's identity independently of the video itself, or to detect that the video was synthetic. Neither happened, and the demands continued until the victim refused one and recognised the pattern.

What is not established is who produced the deepfake or operated the scheme, and the registration of a case under the Information Technology Act is a step in an investigation, not a finding against anyone. The account rests on a single outlet's report.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A security guard in Bengaluru, Ratikanta Giri, aged 29 and originally from Odisha, received a WhatsApp video call on Sept 9. The caller used an AI generated deepfake to appear as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and offered financial aid. A supposed manager then promised Rs 11 lakh, later saying Rs 5 lakh was allotted, and asked Giri to pay processing and other fees. This is the first such case reported in the city.

Giri paid Rs 5,000 as exchange charges, Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN, more than Rs 50,000 as a claimed CBI fine, and further amounts, losing over Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app. When the fraudsters demanded another Rs 50,000, he refused and realized he had been duped. He contacted cybercrime helpline 1930 and then Byappanahalli police. A case was registered under the Information Technology Act, and police urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on them.
